name: Bloom & Bough
tagline: Flowers from Bath, tied by hand

sections.heading: Flowers that mean it
sections.text: Seasonal stems from growers we know, tied the morning you order.

items.title: Weddings
items.text: From a single buttonhole to a whole barn. We visit the venue and plan around the light.

items.title: Weekly bunches
items.text: A bunch on your doorstep every Friday. Pause any week, no questions.

items.title: Workshops
items.text: Two hours, a table of stems, and you leave with something you made.

items.quote: The wedding flowers were better than the pictures I sent them.
items.name: Ella · Widcombe

items.quote: My Friday bunch is the best thing I pay for.
items.name: Tom · Larkhall

items.quote: They taught my daughter to tie a posy and she has not stopped.
items.name: Priya · Oldfield Park

sections.heading: Come and see the shop
sections.text: 12 Walcot Street, open Tuesday to Saturday, nine till six.

sections.heading: It started with a market stall
sections.text: One table on Green Park on Saturdays, and a van that smelled of eucalyptus all week.
sections.text2: Ten years on we have a shop, a walled cutting garden outside the city, and the same rule: nothing flown in when something is growing here.

items.label: Air miles on a Friday bunch

sections.heading: Let’s talk flowers
sections.text: A wedding, a Friday bunch, a question about a plant that is sulking — write and we will answer the same day.

posts.title: What is in season in September
posts.text:
Dahlias, still. Late roses. The first berried stems.

We cut on Mondays and Thursdays, so a Friday bunch has been out of the ground for a day.

posts.title: How to make a bunch last
posts.text: Cut the stems, change the water every two days, and keep it away from the fruit bowl. Ripening fruit gives off a gas that ages flowers.

posts.title: A wedding in a walled garden
posts.text: Two hundred stems of garden roses, all from one grower in Somerset, and a bride who wanted it to look as if nobody had tried.
